value.title: File Upload Restrictions & Execution Resistance Methodology
value.content: {"id": "portswigger_file_upload", "item_type": "methodology", "topic": "file_upload", "category": "PortSwigger Web Security: File Upload Vulnerabilities", "name": "File Upload Restrictions & Execution Resistance Methodology", "cwe": "CWE-434", "owasp_category": "A03:2021 - Injection", "signals": ["unrestricted_file_extension", "client_side_validation_only", "mime_type_spoofing_accepted", "path_traversal_in_filename", "polyglot_file_accepted", "uploaded_file_directly_executable"], "verification_strategy": "Upload benign non-executable test files with varied extensions (.php5, .phtml, .shtml, .jpg.php), test Content-Type header spoofing (e.g. Content-Type: image/jpeg for text file), and test path traversal in the filename attribute (filename='../../test.txt'). Check if files are served from an isolated domain with execution disabled.", "evidence_requirements": ["uploaded_file_url_resolution", "mime_type_override_acceptance", "executable_handler_trigger"], "tools": [{"tool": "AutonomousBrain (Upload Probe)", "cmd": "AutonomousBrain.probe_upload_endpoint(url, file_field)", "desc": "Safely assesses MIME-type, extension blacklists, and path sanitization without webshells"}, {"tool": "ffuf (Upload Fuzzing)", "cmd": "ffuf -u url -F 'file=@test.FUZZ' -w extensions.txt", "desc": "Fuzzes acceptable file extension policies on upload endpoints"}], "remediation": "Validate file extensions against a strict allowlist. Store uploaded files in an isolated object store or dedicated non-executable domain (e.g. AWS S3). Re-encode uploaded images to strip metadata and prevent polyglots.", "description": "PortSwigger File Upload labs explore basic remote code execution via webshell upload, bypassing Content-Type checks, bypassing extension blacklists via secondary extensions or null bytes, and path traversal to place scripts in web roots."}
